brief.headline: AEGIS: found and fixed the bug that made the whole city vanish on iOS, rebuilt the mobile HUD, and replaced the faked roads and welded populations with a real road network, articulated pedestrians, rolling wheels and an animated battle.

items.text: Found why the city disappeared on the owner's iPhone in photoreal mode. buildCity thinned its field to the 430-building budget and then pushed up to six signature towers in AFTER the cut, so it returned 434-436 — 12 of the first 15 sites over. index.html then asked GL to draw more instances than the buffer held. That is INVALID_OPERATION per the WebGL spec: Chrome tolerates it via robust buffer access and reports no error, which is why every desktop and headless test passed, while WebKit drops the whole draw call. Real mode made it total because the wireframe cages that survived in holo are faded to zero there. Fixed at the generator and guarded at the consumer; every skyline is unchanged.

AEGIS mobile HUD. The battle button was invisible: it used a crossed-swords glyph no font in the stack covers, so iOS drew tofu — a red square with an x, which reads as 'close'. Every control is now an SVG icon plus a word and nothing is under a 44px tap target (six of eight were about 20x22). Added COLLAPSE ALL as a floating pill plus per-panel folding: portrait canvas goes from 49.6% of the screen to 53.1%, 60.9% folded, 91.4% hidden. Also fixed the battle strip and every toast printing on top of each other inside the top bar, EXECUTE being unreachable in landscape, crew POV being an inescapable trap on a device with no ESC key, and no safe-area handling at all.

AEGIS roads. The streets were faked twice, independently, and the two fakes disagreed — a painted canvas with no data behind it, and a separate invented lane grid the cars drove on. So traffic ran on invisible lanes unrelated to the visible streets, through buildings. js/roadnet.js is now one directed graph that emits the ribbon mesh, the canvas overlay and the driveable lanes from the same nodes, laid out on the half-offsets of the building block step. Arterials and streets, signals, bridges, left-hand traffic. Zero buildings standing in a carriageway.

AEGIS locomotion. Pedestrians were one welded mesh and slid with a sine bob; all four wheels of every car were merged into one geometry, so a wheel could not physically turn. Five instanced parts now give a real walk cycle whose phase advances with DISTANCE TRAVELLED rather than the clock, and four instanced wheels per car roll off distance covered and steer off path curvature. Speeds were 2.5-6.6 m/s for a shopping crowd and 14-32 m/s for city traffic; both are honest now. The work surfaced that the merged person faced +X while the app rotates walkers to face +Z — the entire crowd had been walking sideways.

AEGIS battle animation. The sim was correct and inert: a killed unit simply stopped being drawn. Deaths are now animated and permanent — armour slumps, chars and smokes where it died, infantry fall, a downed Apache windmills in. Wrecks persist so the battlefield accumulates history. Guns recoil and kick a blast plume, hulls lean into turns and squat under power, tracked vehicles throw dust. New pooled fx module, fixed-size, no allocation in the frame loop.

AEGIS render modes: one scene graph, two complete looks. HOLO is the tactical projection; REAL is a lit world with sky gradient, distance fog, sun and bounce fill, draped asphalt streets and models in their authored colours. Modes swap material state, never geometry, so toggling is instant and the simulation cannot desync. Every material registers once with a role, so anything added later gets both looks for free. Button, or H.

AEGIS crew POV: during a battle, tap a unit or press [ / ] and the camera flies from the table into that crew's head over 1.15 s. Helmet-cam framing with the table UI cleared, live HP, heading and range to that unit's own target, and a signal-lost hand-back when the crew is killed. Eye height comes from the unit class, so a prone sniper, a tank commander in the hatch and an Apache pilot are all at their real heights. Cycling walks the combined-arms picture: nine presses gives pilot, tank commander, IFV gunner, vehicle commander, gun chief, launcher crew, gunner, sniper, rifleman.

AEGIS landmarks: 18 structures authored in real metres and merged to one geometry each — Golden Gate, Salesforce, Liberty, Empire State, Eiffel, Fuji, Skytree, Elizabeth Tower, Colosseum, Giza, Opera House, Burj Khalifa, Christ the Redeemer, Taj Mahal, Sagrada Família, capitol, plus generic tower and peak fallbacks. Twelve destinations place them at real offsets from the city centre; the landmark the intel panel names is the one wired to the strike and BDA path, and the rest topple too.
